analysis|10-05|1988|Το «Όχι» στον Πινοσέτ|The No vote against Pinochet|After the dictatorship of Pinochet, which had been established by the coup of 1973, the regime remained in power for decades with violent repression of the opposition. The constitution of 1980 provided for a referendum on its continuation. This provision was part of the institutional construction of the regime. // On 5 October 1988 the referendum took place, where voters were asked to answer "yes" or "no" to the extension of Pinochet's power for eight years. The majority voted "no", and the regime acknowledged the defeat. // The result opened the way to free elections the following year and to the return of democracy to Chile. The referendum remains in history as a symbol of peaceful change and of the power of the popular vote.

analysis|10-06|1973|Αρχίζει ο Πόλεμος του Γιομ Κιπούρ|The Yom Kippur War begins|After the Six-Day War of 1967, Israel held territories of Egypt, Syria and Jordan. Egypt and Syria sought to recover their territories, and tensions were high without a diplomatic solution. // On 6 October 1973, on the day of Yom Kippur, Egyptian and Syrian forces attacked Israeli positions in the Sinai and on the Golan Heights. The attack took Israel by surprise, and it responded with mobilization. The battles lasted about three weeks, with great losses on both sides. // The war ended with a ceasefire agreed with the mediation of the United States and the Soviet Union. The conflict led to the gradual rapprochement of Egypt and Israel, which ended in the peace agreement of 1979, and showed the importance of diplomacy in the Middle East.

analysis|10-06|1981|Δολοφονείται ο Ανουάρ Σαντάτ|Anwar Sadat is assassinated|Anwar Sadat, successor of Nasser, had signed peace with Israel in 1979, which provoked intense reaction in part of the Arab world. In Egypt, opponents of the agreement, especially Islamic groups and officers, accused the leadership of concessions. // On 6 October 1981, during a military parade in Cairo for the anniversary of the 1973 war, members of an Islamic organization opened fire and killed the president. The murder took place within a few minutes, and several officials were wounded. // Hosni Mubarak took his place and maintained the agreement with Israel. The murder revealed the internal tensions of Egypt, while peace with Israel remained stable for decades.

analysis|10-07|1949|Ιδρύεται η Ανατολική Γερμανία|East Germany is founded|After the Second World War Germany was divided into occupation zones by the victorious powers. The Western allies and the Soviet Union disagreed about the future of the country, and the division intensified as each side promoted its own administration. // On 7 October 1949 the German Democratic Republic was founded in the Soviet zone, after the establishment of the Federal Republic in the western zone in May of the same year. The new state operated under Soviet influence, with the leadership of the communist party. // The founding of the Democratic Republic contributed to the lasting division of Germany and of Berlin, which lasted until 1990. The Berlin Wall, built in 1961, became the symbol of this division.

analysis|10-07|2001|Οι ΗΠΑ επιτίθενται στο Αφγανιστάν|The United States attacks Afghanistan|After the attacks of 11 September 2001 on the United States, the American government blamed al-Qaeda, which had bases in Afghanistan, and demanded that the Taliban regime hand it over. The refusal of the Taliban led to political and military preparations. // On 7 October 2001 the United States, with the participation of Britain, began air bombardments on targets of the Taliban and al-Qaeda. The operation, named Enduring Freedom, was accompanied by action of Afghan forces on the ground, and within a few weeks it led to the fall of the Taliban regime in Kabul. // The war began a long military presence that lasted two decades, with significant losses and political developments. The operation is a turning point in American foreign policy after 11 September, with consequences for the stability of the region.

analysis|10-08|1871|Ξεσπά η Μεγάλη Πυρκαγιά του Σικάγου|The Great Chicago Fire breaks out|In the mid-19th century Chicago was a rapidly growing city, with wooden buildings and dense construction. Industry and the railway had made it a transport center, but drought and the lack of effective firefighting made it vulnerable. // On 8 October 1871 a fire broke out in a shed, and the flames spread quickly through the neighborhoods, with strong winds. The fire lasted two days, destroyed a large part of the city, killed hundreds of people and left about one hundred thousand residents homeless. // The fire led to the rebuilding of the city with more resistant materials, such as brick, stone and iron, and it reshaped the architecture of Chicago. The reconstruction made the city one of the most important urban centers of the United States.

analysis|10-09|1874|Ιδρύεται η Παγκόσμια Ταχυδρομική Ένωση|The Universal Postal Union is founded|On 9 October 1874 the treaty founding the General Postal Union, later renamed the Universal Postal Union, was signed in Bern. In the 19th century postal communication between countries was complicated, with different rules, fees and routes. This agreement was necessary for international communication. // The agreement established common rules for the processing and transport of mail among the member states. These rules simplified international correspondence. // The Union is one of the oldest international organizations and continues to coordinate world postal services. 9 October is celebrated as World Post Day, in honor of the founding of the organization.

analysis|10-09|1962|Η Ουγκάντα γίνεται ανεξάρτητη|Uganda becomes independent|Uganda was a British protectorate in East Africa, with tensions between traditional kingdoms and political parties. In the 1950s movements for self-government developed, and local leaders negotiated the terms of independence. // On 9 October 1962 Uganda became an independent state, with the colonial administration handing power over to the local government. The new state started as a constitutional monarchy, with the traditional kingdoms keeping an important role in politics. // The independence of Uganda did not lead to stability, as political crises and military coups followed. The history of the country shows the difficulties of decolonization, but also the endurance of local societies.

analysis|10-09|1963|Η καταστροφή του φράγματος Βαγιόντ|The Vajont Dam disaster|In the 1950s Italy was building dams for energy production, and in the Vajont valley a high dam was built that created an artificial lake. The area had geological problems, and several experts had warned of the danger of landslides. // On 9 October 1963 a huge mass of rock and soil fell into the lake, and the wave that was created went over the dam and destroyed villages of the valley, such as Longarone. The disaster killed almost two thousand people. // The tragedy revealed the responsibilities of the company and of the authorities, who had ignored the warnings. It led to stricter rules for dams and remains a symbol of the need for the prevention of technological disasters.

analysis|10-09|1967|Εκτελείται ο Τσε Γκεβάρα|Che Guevara is executed|On 9 October 1967 Ernesto Che Guevara, an Argentine doctor, was executed by a Bolivian soldier in the village of La Higuera. Che had taken part in the Cuban revolution of 1959 and had been a significant figure of the government. In 1965 he left Cuba to organize revolutionary movements in other countries of Latin America. // Che was captured in Bolivia in October 1967. The operation had been supported by American intelligence services. // His death became a symbol for many movements of the era, and his figure remains controversial. Che is associated with anti-imperialist ideology, but also with harsh acts of the Cuban revolution, and the discussion about his role continues.

analysis|10-10|1911|Η Εξέγερση της Ουτσάνγκ|The Wuchang Uprising|On 10 October 1911 soldiers in the city of Wuchang rebelled, took control of the area and began the revolution that became known as the Xinhai Revolution. The Qing Empire was in deep crisis at the beginning of the 20th century, with financial problems, foreign influence and discontent over concessions to foreigners. Revolutionary organizations, such as the Tongmenghui of Sun Yat-sen, demanded the overthrow of the dynasty and a republic. // The uprising spread quickly to other provinces, and the movement took on national dimensions within a few months. The speed of the spread surprised the government. // The Revolution led to the overthrow of the empire and to the proclamation of the Republic of China the following year. The event closed a long period of imperial power and opened an era of political instability and conflict.

analysis|10-10|1913|Ανατινάζεται το φράγμα Γκαμπόα|The Gamboa dam is blown up|In the early 20th century France and the United States were considering ways to connect the two oceans, with the Panama Canal as the great project of the era. The United States undertook its construction in 1904, after an agreement with the new republic of Panama. // On 10 October 1913 the Gamboa dam was blown up, a temporary dam that held back the waters in a section of the canal, with an electrical signal given by President Woodrow Wilson from Washington. The waters flooded the channel and so the two oceans were joined over a large part of the route. // The completion of the canal, in 1914, changed navigation and world trade, since ships no longer had to sail around the southern tip of America. The canal remains vital for international transport.

analysis|10-10|1964|Οι Ολυμπιακοί Αγώνες του Τόκιο|The Tokyo Olympic Games|Japan had recovered from the devastation of the Second World War and achieved rapid economic growth. The choice of Tokyo as the host city of the 1964 Olympic Games was a symbol of the country's return to the international stage. // On 10 October 1964 the opening ceremony took place at the National Stadium in Tokyo. The Games were broadcast live by satellite to many countries, and this transmission made sport accessible to millions of viewers around the world. // The Tokyo Games are regarded as a turning point for the image of Japan and for international television. They contributed to the development of the country's infrastructure, such as the Shinkansen railway system, which was inaugurated shortly before the Games.

analysis|10-11|1899|Αρχίζει ο Δεύτερος Πόλεμος των Μπόερ|The Second Boer War begins|At the end of the 19th century Britain wanted control of South Africa, rich in gold and diamonds, while the Boer republics resisted. Tensions over the rights of British settlers and over political autonomy were increasing. // On 11 October 1899 the two Boer republics declared war on Britain, and their forces invaded the British possessions in the area. At first the Boers won several victories, but the British counteroffensive, with a large army, changed the course of the conflict. // The war lasted almost three years and ended in 1902 with the Treaty of Vereeniging, which gave Britain control of the two republics. The war left deep marks, with the use of concentration camps and the destruction of farming areas.

analysis|10-11|1922|Υπογράφεται η ανακωχή των Μουδανιών|The Armistice of Mudanya is signed|After the Asia Minor Catastrophe of 1922, the Greek army had withdrawn from Asia Minor, and Kemal's Turkey had prevailed in the area. The question of Eastern Thrace and of the Straits remained open, and the Allies had to decide the future of the area. // On 11 October 1922 an armistice was signed at Mudanya between the Allies, Britain, France and Italy, and the Turkish government of Ankara. The agreement provided for the withdrawal of the Greek forces from Eastern Thrace and the conduct of negotiations for peace. // The armistice was the beginning of the Treaty of Lausanne of 1923, which set the borders of modern Turkey and provided for the exchange of populations. That exchange left deep marks on Greek and Turkish society.

analysis|10-11|1962|Αρχίζει η Β΄ Σύνοδος του Βατικανού|The Second Vatican Council begins|In the 20th century the Catholic Church faced the challenges of the modern era, as secular culture and liturgical tradition were changing. Pope John XXIII sought renewal and dialogue with the modern world. // On 11 October 1962 Pope John XXIII opened the Second Vatican Ecumenical Council in Rome, which brought together bishops from all over the world. The discussions concerned the liturgy, the relation of the Church with the world and the unity of Christians. // The Council, which concluded in 1965, led to important changes, such as the use of the local language in worship and greater participation of the faithful. Its legacy still influences the life of the Catholic Church.

analysis|10-11|1968|Εκτοξεύεται ο Apollo 7|Apollo 7 is launched|After the tragedy of Apollo 1 in 1967, when three astronauts died in a fire, the Apollo program was under review. NASA wanted to test the new systems of the spacecraft in orbit around the Earth before the mission to the Moon. // On 11 October 1968 Apollo 7 was launched, with three astronauts on board. It was the first crewed mission of the program and it flew in orbit around the Earth for eleven days, testing the systems of the capsule. // The mission proved that the capsule was reliable and opened the way for the Apollo 8 and Apollo 11 missions, which reached the Moon. It is regarded as a milestone for modern space engineering.

analysis|10-12|1492|Ο Χριστόφορος Κολόμβος φτάνει στην Αμερική|Christopher Columbus reaches America|At the end of the 15th century Europe was seeking sea routes to Asia, to obtain Asian products and spices without the intermediaries of trade. Christopher Columbus believed that he could reach Asia by sailing west, and he asked for support from European courts. // With funding from Spain, Columbus set out with three ships and on 12 October 1492 reached an island of the Bahamas, which he named San Salvador. He himself believed he was near Asia, while the Europeans called the inhabitants of the islands "Indians", because of the confusion about geography. // The arrival of Columbus opened the way for European colonization of the Americas, with consequences that deeply affected the peoples of the region, their population, economy and politics. The history of the voyage is discussed to this day, because it reflects both scientific curiosity and the violence of colonialism.

analysis|10-12|1968|Ανεξαρτησία της Ισημερινής Γουινέας|Independence of Equatorial Guinea|Spanish Guinea was a colony in West Africa, with islands and a mainland part. In the 1960s the political forces of the region demanded independence, and Spain accepted the gradual transition to self-government. // On 12 October 1968 the country became an independent state, with Francisco Macías Nguema as its first president. The transition soon led to internal conflicts and to a government with authoritarian features. // The independence of Equatorial Guinea was linked with one of the most authoritarian governments in Africa, and later with the development of the oil industry. The country still faces challenges regarding human rights and economic inequality.

analysis|10-13|54|Ο Νέρωνας γίνεται αυτοκράτορας|Nero becomes emperor|The Roman Empire of the 1st century AD succeeded the emperor Claudius, who ruled from 41 to 54. The succession was the subject of intense conflicts at court, and Agrippina, wife of Claudius, sought to secure power for her son from a previous marriage. // After the death of Claudius, Nero, then 16 years old, was proclaimed emperor on 13 October 54 AD. The first days of his reign were guided by his mother, by Seneca and by Burrus, who tried to control policy. // The beginning of Nero's reign is regarded as relatively mild, with the policy of the first years influenced by his advisers. Later his reign became particularly authoritarian, and Nero was linked with many controversial acts that shaped his image in history.

analysis|10-13|1307|Η σύλληψη των Ναϊτών|The arrest of the Templars|The Order of the Knights Templar had been founded in the 12th century to protect pilgrims in the Holy Land, and had acquired great wealth and influence in Europe. King Philip IV of France had large financial debts to it, and wished to control the order. // On 13 October 1307 the French authorities arrested the knights of the order in France, on charges of heresy and other offences. Many knights were interrogated, and their property partly passed to the crown. // In 1312 Pope Clement V formally dissolved the order, although the trial had strongly political motives. The case is regarded as an example of the relation between power and religion, and its link with the tradition of Friday the 13th is later and is not fully documented.

analysis|10-13|1923|Η Άγκυρα γίνεται πρωτεύουσα|Ankara becomes the capital|After the collapse of the Ottoman Empire, Constantinople was under Allied occupation, while the movement of Mustafa Kemal was organizing the new Turkish national government in Ankara. Ankara, in the heart of Anatolia, had already been chosen as the seat of the National Assembly. // On 13 October 1923 the Grand National Assembly of Turkey proclaimed Ankara the capital of the state, instead of Constantinople. The decision was linked with the symbolic end of the Ottoman era and with the search for a new national identity. // The transfer of the capital expresses the break with the Ottoman past and the effort for a national state centered in Anatolia. Ankara developed into a modern city, and the decision remains an important point in the history of modern Turkey.

analysis|10-13|1943|Η Ιταλία κηρύσσει πόλεμο στη Γερμανία|Italy declares war on Germany|After the conclusion of the armistice with the Allies in September 1943, the Italian government of Pietro Badoglio found itself in a different position toward Germany, which had already occupied a large part of the country. The Italian government sought to free itself from German influence. // On 13 October 1943 Italy declared war on Germany, after its change of camp. The decision strengthened the international position of the government toward the Allies, but northern Italy remained under German occupation and the battles continued. // The declaration of war showed the overturning of Italian alliances and opened a period of division in the country, between the south under the Allies and the north under Germany and the Fascist Italian Social Republic. This period led to the final defeat of the Fascist regime in 1945.

analysis|10-14|1066|Η μάχη του Χέιστινγκς|The Battle of Hastings|After the victory of Harold over Harald Hardrada at Stamford Bridge, the king of England hastened south to face William, who had landed on the coast. The army of Harold was tired from the march and was smaller than the Norman one. // On 14 October 1066 the two armies clashed near Hastings. The battle lasted for hours, with the Normans using archers and cavalry, and Harold was killed. William's victory opened the way to control of the country. // The Battle of Hastings is regarded as a landmark in the history of England and of Europe, because it changed the administration, the language and the social structures of the country. William, known as the Conqueror, was crowned king at Westminster in December 1066.

analysis|10-14|1947|Ο Τσακ Γιέγκερ σπάει το φράγμα του ήχου|Chuck Yeager breaks the sound barrier|After the Second World War aviation technology was pushing speed limits, and the "sound barrier" was a challenge for engineers. American services developed experimental aircraft, such as the Bell X-1, to study flight conditions at supersonic speeds. // On 14 October 1947 the pilot Chuck Yeager flew the Bell X-1 and exceeded the speed of sound for the first time, over the desert of California. The aircraft had been released from a bomber during the flight. // Yeager's flight opened the way for supersonic aircraft and the development of modern aeronautics. This achievement is regarded as a milestone of aviation history, and Yeager is recognized as one of the most important test pilots of the era.

analysis|10-14|1962|Ξεκινά η κρίση των πυραύλων της Κούβας|The Cuban missile crisis begins|After the revolution of 1959 Cuba allied with the Soviet Union, and the United States was worried about Soviet influence at its doorstep. The American invasion at the Bay of Pigs in 1961 had failed, and Moscow wanted to protect the Cuban government. // On 14 October 1962 an American U-2 spy plane photographed the installations of Soviet missiles in Cuba. The discovery led to a week of intensive consultations, and the world faced the danger of nuclear war, since the missiles could strike a large part of the United States. // The missile crisis ended with an agreement between Kennedy and Khrushchev, with the withdrawal of the Soviet missiles from Cuba and the commitment of the United States not to invade the island. The crisis is a leading example of nuclear deterrence and of the need for dialogue.

analysis|10-14|1964|Ο Μάρτιν Λούθερ Κινγκ παίρνει το Νόμπελ Ειρήνης|Martin Luther King receives the Nobel Peace Prize|In the 1960s Martin Luther King was the main leader of the movement for the civil rights of African Americans. The movement used non-violent resistance, with demonstrations, campaigns and legal appeals, and tensions with the authorities were intense. // On 14 October 1964 King was honored with the Nobel Peace Prize, at the age of 35, and was the youngest laureate up to then. The committee recognized his contribution to the struggle for equality and non-violence. // The prize gave international emphasis to the struggle of African Americans and strengthened the political pressure for legislative change, such as the Civil Rights Act of 1964. King's legacy today is a symbol of non-violence and equality.

analysis|10-15|1582|Εφαρμόζεται για πρώτη φορά το Γρηγοριανό ημερολόγιο|The Gregorian calendar is applied for the first time|In the 16th century the Julian calendar had accumulated an error, and the date of Easter and of the feasts was gradually shifting in relation to the seasons. Pope Gregory XIII commissioned a study for the correction, and the reform was based on astronomical calculations. // On 15 October 1582 the Gregorian calendar was applied for the first time in Italy, in Spain and in Portugal, with the omission of ten days, so that the day after 4 October was the 15th. The change was made to adjust the dates to the solar year. // The reform was not accepted immediately throughout Europe, and many countries, among them Orthodox ones, adopted it with a delay. The Gregorian calendar is today the dominant one worldwide, while the difference between the calendars continues to concern some churches.

analysis|10-15|1815|Ο Ναπολέων φτάνει στην Αγία Ελένη|Napoleon arrives at Saint Helena|After the defeat at Waterloo in June 1815, Napoleon abdicated and tried to leave for the United States. The British, who had defeated Napoleon together with the Prussians, decided to exile him to a remote island. // On 15 October 1815 Napoleon arrived at Saint Helena, a volcanic island in the Atlantic, far from Europe and Africa. There he lived under strict surveillance until his death in 1821, with constant complaints about the conditions of his life. // The exile of Napoleon closed a turbulent period of European history, and the Congress of Vienna had already shaped a new balance of powers in Europe. Saint Helena became a symbol of the fall of a great leader and of his memory.

analysis|10-15|1917|Εκτελείται η Μάτα Χάρι|Mata Hari is executed|During the First World War Europe was steeped in espionage and suspicion. Margaretha Zelle, known as Mata Hari, was a Dutch dancer who lived in Paris and had been linked with officials of many countries. Her fame made her an easy target for suspicion. // She herself was accused of spying for Germany and was tried by a French military tribunal. She was sentenced to death, and on 15 October 1917 she was shot at Vincennes, near Paris. Her guilt has not been adequately documented to this day. // Her case became a symbol of the suspicion of war and of the myth of the multifaceted spy. Her story continues to inspire works of art and books, and the attribution of responsibility remains a subject of discussion.

analysis|10-15|1940|Η Ιταλία αποφασίζει επίθεση κατά της Ελλάδας|Italy decides to attack Greece|In mid-1940, with France defeated and Britain isolated, Benito Mussolini wished to demonstrate Italian military power and to secure new territories in the Mediterranean. Greece, under Ioannis Metaxas, remained neutral and wary of Italian ambitions. // At a meeting in Rome in October 1940, the Italian leadership decided on the invasion of Greece. The attack began on 28 October from Albania, and the Italian army advanced into the Greek interior, where however it met strong resistance. // The Italian attack failed, and the Greek army overturned the Italian positions, in a victory that became a milestone for Greece. This failure is linked with the later German intervention in the Balkans.

analysis|10-15|2003|Η Κίνα στέλνει άνθρωπο στο διάστημα|China sends a man into space|After the end of the Cold War space race, many countries were developing their own launch capabilities. China, which had developed a space program since the 1970s, sought to acquire human spaceflight capability, so as to follow the United States and Russia. // On 15 October 2003 China launched Shenzhou 5 with the astronaut Yang Liwei, who made a flight in orbit around the Earth for about twenty hours. The mission was the first Chinese crewed flight, and China became the third country to send a human into space with its own means. // The success of the mission strengthened China's prestige in technology and showed its ambitions for future missions. The event is regarded as a milestone for Chinese science and for international space activity.

analysis|10-16|1793|Αποκεφαλίζεται η Μαρία Αντουανέτα|Marie Antoinette is beheaded|Marie Antoinette, wife of Louis XVI, was the object of intense resentment during the Revolution, and was regarded by many as a symbol of the luxury of the court. After the storming of the Tuileries and the imprisonment of the royal family in 1792, her trial began before the revolutionary tribunal. // On 16 October 1793 Marie Antoinette was executed by guillotine in Paris, after a trial that had sentenced her for treason. Her execution took place in a period of intense political extremism in France. // Her execution linked the Revolution with the phase of the Terror, while the figure of the queen remains a subject of historical analysis. The interpretation of her life is shaped by the political and social criticism of each era.

analysis|10-16|1946|Εκτελούνται οι καταδικασμένοι της Νυρεμβέργης|The Nuremberg convicts are executed|After the conclusion of the trial at Nuremberg, the verdicts provided for death sentences for some defendants. The Allies decided on the execution of those sentenced to death, while some of the defendants had already taken their own lives. // On 16 October 1946 ten Nazi leaders were hanged in the Nuremberg prison, after the decision of the International Military Tribunal. Among those executed were Joachim von Ribbentrop, as well as leading figures of the government and the military forces. // The executions marked the end of the first great international trial for war crimes and established the principle that responsibility for war crimes is individual. The legacy of the trial continues to influence international criminal law.

analysis|10-16|1964|Η πρώτη κινεζική πυρηνική δοκιμή|China's first nuclear test|In the 1960s China faced serious threats from the United States and the Soviet Union, and its leadership decided to develop its own nuclear arsenal. The break with Moscow had already grown sharp, and the need for autonomy in defense was pressing. // On 16 October 1964 China carried out its first nuclear test at Lop Nur, in the western part of the country. The country thus became the fifth to possess a nuclear weapon, after the United States, the Soviet Union, the United Kingdom and France. // The test increased China's geopolitical weight and changed the balance of power in Asia. It also led to international efforts to control nuclear weapons, which later contributed to the Non-Proliferation Treaty.

analysis|10-16|1978|Ο Καρόλ Βοϊτύλα γίνεται Πάπας|Karol Wojtyla becomes Pope|In recent years the Catholic Church had been in a transitional period, after the death of Pope John Paul I in September 1978, a few weeks after his election. The college of cardinals gathered in the Vatican to elect a new pope. // On 16 October 1978 the Polish cardinal Karol Wojtyla was elected pope with the name John Paul II. He was the first non-Italian pope since 1523, that is, after 455 years, and his election was regarded as historic. // John Paul II was one of the most widely travelled popes, and the political dimension of his course contributed to the changes in Eastern Europe. His papacy became a point of reference for dialogue with other religions.

analysis|10-17|1777|Η παράδοση του Σαρατόγκα|The surrender at Saratoga|During the American Revolutionary War, the British strategy included the seizure of the Hudson River valley, to separate the American colonies. General John Burgoyne began a campaign from Canada toward Albany, with an army that included British, German mercenaries and native allies. // On 17 October 1777, after two battles at Saratoga, Burgoyne surrendered to the Americans under Horatio Gates. The surrender of an entire British army was an important victory for the revolutionaries, and it strengthened French support for the United States. // The battle of Saratoga is regarded as a turning point of the war, since it showed that the Americans could defeat the British army. The French alliance contributed decisively to the final victory at Yorktown in 1781.

analysis|10-17|1806|Δολοφονείται ο Ντεσαλίν|Dessalines is assassinated|Haiti was the first country of Latin America and the Caribbean to win its independence after a slave revolution, in 1804. Jean-Jacques Dessalines was the first leader of the independent country, and his government was marked by authoritarianism and the execution of political opponents. // On 17 October 1806 Dessalines was assassinated near Pont-Rouge, outside the capital, in an ambush organized by his political opponents. The murder left a power vacuum, and the country was divided into a northern and a southern part with different leaders. // The country was divided for several years, and Dessalines remains an important figure of Haitian history, as a symbol of independence and of the conflict over power. His memory is honored as part of the national identity of Haiti.

analysis|10-17|1979|Νόμπελ Ειρήνης στη Μητέρα Τερέζα|The Nobel Peace Prize to Mother Teresa|Albanian nun Teresa, known as Mother Teresa, had founded in 1950 in Calcutta a community for the care of the poor and the sick. Her work spread to many countries, and her life in the Indian city made her known as a symbol of humanitarian care. // On 17 October 1979 Mother Teresa was honored with the Nobel Peace Prize for her work with the poorest people. The committee noted her care for the weak, while she herself asked that no official banquet be held for the prize, and that the money be given to the poor. // The prize strengthened the international profile of the work of her missions, which operate in many countries. Her legacy is still discussed today, with criticism of the conditions in some institutions, but also with respect for her care for the marginalized.

analysis|10-17|1989|Ο σεισμός του Λόμα Πρίιτα|The Loma Prieta earthquake|In the late 1980s California was an area with active faults, such as the San Andreas fault. The San Francisco area had a history of seismic tremors, and the residents knew the danger, although many buildings were not always reinforced. // On 17 October 1989, during the third game of the baseball World Series, an earthquake of magnitude 6.9 on the Richter scale struck the area. The game was interrupted, damage was caused to bridges, highways and buildings, and dozens of people were killed. // The earthquake highlighted the need for modern earthquake engineering and for the upgrading of bridges and infrastructure. The event remained in the memory of the residents, and the experience helped in the development of better safety rules for the buildings of California.

analysis|10-18|1081|Η μάχη του Δυρραχίου|The Battle of Dyrrhachium|At the end of the 11th century the Norman Robert Guiscard, based in southern Italy, sought to conquer part of the Byzantine lands in the Balkans. The Byzantine Empire, under Alexios I Komnenos, faced multiple threats and was seeking allies. // On 18 October 1081 the army of Alexios was defeated by the Normans near Dyrrhachium, on the shores of the Adriatic. The victory opened the way for the Normans into the interior of the Balkans, although the operation did not lead to a permanent conquest of the area. // The Battle of Dyrrhachium was important for Byzantine history, because it showed the need to strengthen the army and its alliances. Alexios later managed to recover, and the event is remembered as a turning point in the relations of Byzantium with the West.

analysis|10-18|1867|Οι ΗΠΑ παραλαμβάνουν την Αλάσκα|The United States takes possession of Alaska|In the 19th century the Russian Empire held Alaska, but the remote region was difficult to govern and had no great economic importance for Russia. The Russian government considered the possibility of selling it, in order to avoid the risk of losing it in a possible conflict. // On 18 October 1867 the transfer of Alaska to the United States was completed, in exchange for 7.2 million dollars.
